newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: INTERVIEW - Forbes says growth on cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Forbes says growth on cost cuts.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Forbes Ceylon Ltd said on Monday net profits for the 1996/97 financial year (April-March) rose sharply, mostly as a result of shedding unprofitable businesses in the past two years.

The firm, the holding company of a group which is involved in food, services, plantations, property and investments, said net profit after tax rose 681 percent to 88.59 million rupees ($1.5 million) from 11.34 million on turnover of 776.98 million rupees.

"In the 1994-95 financial year we took a decision to divest anything that did not look steady and emphasise budgetary controls and accountability," Nissanka de Mel, financial controller of Forbes Ceylon told Reuters.
"As a result, the company is now systems-driven and not people-driven," he added.

Forbes Ceylon went public in August 1994 when Canada's Ondaatje Corporation -- now Global Equity Corporation -- bought a 50 percent stake in the company. It has an issued capital of 2.4 billion rupees comprising 240 million 10-rupee shares.
The first area to come under scrutiny was the company's food sector which included Soy Food Ltd, a cannery and confectionery. The company has shed all but Soy Food.
Forbes Marketing, another arm of the company, was sold in the 1995/96 financial year, de Mel said.

The service sector was trimmed and its main activity now is operating a warehousing service on a property owned by Forbes Real Estate. It also supplies packing material and dolomite to the tea sector, and exports gherkins and spices.
Associate Forbes & Walker, which is active in tea, commodities and stock broking, has been profitable due to buoyant tea prices.
Forbes Ceylon is also the general sales agent in Sri Lanka for Emirates Airlines. The company was an unsuccessful bidder for yet-to-be-listed Balagoda Plantations Ltd.
"Our operations are all streamlined and doing well now, but future growth in earnings depends on the deployment of the firm's large pool of cash resources," said de Mel.
A sum of 1.1 billion rupees of shareholders funds is being held offshore by Forbes Capital, a fully owned subsidiary.
Analysts say the company's investments have been slowed down due to a takeover bid by Vanik Incorporation Ltd, which said it intends making an offer for controlling interest in Forbes Ceylon.
